raw:
I answered from prior knowledge of NAS-Bench-201 behavior rather than running anything, so these are rough estimates, not computed values.

The main considerations were:
- An edit that adds a strong op (conv) helps less when the paths it feeds are already well supplied. Interaction is therefore often negative, or at least not consistently positive across all three datasets.
- Edge 4 and edge 5 matter most because they feed the output node. Edges 3, 4 and 5 are the output edges.
- Removing edge 1 (setting it to none) hurts less when other paths into node 2 and node 3 are strong. A parent that is a conv or skip on the path therefore tends to lower the effect rather than raise it.
- Claims 19 and 27 say edge 4 is the edit target and also the parent. Those conditions describe the op being replaced. Replacing skip with conv_3x3 should give a bigger gain than replacing other ops, since skip is weak. Replacing avg_pool with conv_3x3 should also give a large gain, though less reliably.
- Claim 20 describes replacing avg_pool on edge 0 with none. This likely hurts more than replacing other ops, so the effect is lower under the condition.
- Most other claims are near the noise level, so I kept them low.
